introduction: Colorado LEAP helps eligible households with part of their winter heating costs. The 2026–2027 application season begins November 1, 2026 and ends April 30, 2027.
description: Colorado LEAP helps eligible households with part of their winter heating costs. The 2026–2027 application season begins November 1, 2026 and ends April 30, 2027.

sections.who: Applicants must pay home heating costs, directly or through rent, and meet income and lawful-presence requirements. Renters may qualify; disclose whether housing is subsidized and how heating is paid.
sections.get: LEAP usually pays the heating supplier rather than the household. It does not cover the entire winter bill or portable heaters. Heating-system repair support is a separate related service.
sections.docs:
• Recent heating bill, or rent receipt showing heating costs.
  • Previous month’s household income and self-employment expense records.
  • Household birth dates, Social Security numbers and requested lawful-presence records.
sections.apply:
1. Apply during the season

    Use the PEAK link on the LEAP page, or obtain a paper application from your county office. Call 866-432-8435 for help.

  2. Submit a complete signed application

    Attach readable records and send them to the correct county. Missing answers or income evidence can delay processing.

  3. Report a heating emergency

    Call 866-432-8435 if heat will be shut off or fuel is running out. Keep paying bills and contact the supplier about payment arrangements.
sections.after: Watch for the decision notice showing the benefit and recipient. Call HEAT-HELP to ask about status or other utility support.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using LEAP eligibility, season and application instructions. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: When does the current season open?
Can heat included in rent count?
It can; supply a recent rent receipt and explain the heating arrangement and subsidy status.
Should I stop paying the bill?
No. Continue payments and discuss overdue bills with the supplier.
No. The state excludes temporary or portable heating sources.
Is a furnace problem the same application?
Ask HEAT-HELP about the related heating-system repair or replacement program.
